solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Contributed short retrospective for literary collection

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its end, so the last letter goes
a retrospective looks backwards, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: to contribute something is to add it

explanation.surface: A writer contributed a short look back to an anthology of literature.
explanation.walkthrough: ADDED loses its final D to give ADDE, which read backwards gives EDDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are the two medieval Icelandic compilations of Norse myth and poetry, a classic body of old writings.

clue.text: See 28
Setter has dessert with dram brought round plane

indicators.note: bringing something round another wraps it about, so one piece goes outside the rest

blocks.note: the setter says 'I have', contracted to I've
a bombe is a moulded frozen dessert
dr is the standard abbreviation for dram

explanation.surface: The setter is enjoying a pudding with a whisky passed round after it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter has' is the setter saying 'I have', contracted. A bombe is a dome-shaped frozen pudding; dr is the apothecaries' abbreviation for dram.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive-bomber is a type of military aircraft that releases its bombs while diving steeply at the target.

clue.text: Short time after ditching university, daughter gets rich

indicators.note: to ditch something is to throw it away, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a minute is a short time
U is the abbreviation for university
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter drops out of university and soon strikes it rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short time' looks like it is being shortened, but it is a whole unit of time that loses the university letter. 'Minted' is British slang for very wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang someone minted has lots of money, as if they could print their own coins.

clue.text: Where Bowie died, before noon, in a hotel that rocks

indicators.note: something that rocks is shaken about, so its letters are jumbled
one thing being in another means it is placed inside

blocks.note: a.m. means before noon
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: It suggests David Bowie dying one morning in a rock-and-roll hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bowie is not the singer but Jim Bowie, the frontiersman killed defending the Alamo in 1836. AM goes inside a jumble of A HOTEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Jim Bowie was killed at the Alamo mission in San Antonio during the Texan revolution's famous siege of 1836.

clue.text: Southern brother seen in Burberry occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A southern gentleman's brother is spotted wearing a Burberry coat now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Burberry is a British fashion house known for trench coats. Brer is the Southern US dialect form familiar from the Uncle Remus stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Brer is a dialect contraction of brother from the American South, as in the folk character Brer Rabbit.

clue.text: Settler – one swimming in German city, did you say?

indicators.note: asking whether you said something points to how the words are spoken rather than written

blocks.note: a swimmer in Cologne could be a Cologne eel

explanation.surface: A settler asks about someone swimming in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimmer is a fish, an eel, and the German city is Cologne; say 'Cologne eel' quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonial, used as a noun, is an inhabitant of a colony, typically one who came out from the mother country.

clue.text: Permission to enter a social event: need hand to gain access?

indicators.note: gaining access means getting inside, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: taken as written
a dance is a social event
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: To get into a party you need someone to lend a hand with entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The hand is slang, as in 'get your mitts off', and it enters the event just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Admittance is the right or act of being allowed in to a place, which is exactly leave to go inside.

clue.text: Piping insulated by copper covering in India

indicators.note: something insulated is wrapped up inside a layer, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a copper is a policeman, and DI is a detective inspector
piping hot means very hot

explanation.surface: It sounds like pipework lagged with copper cladding in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like the metal but is slang for a police officer, here a DI. 'Piping' is HOT, as in piping hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the loincloth worn by many Hindu men, a length of cloth wrapped round the waist and legs.

clue.text: 16 Across writer is with bestial crowd outside court

indicators.note: one thing outside another surrounds it, so a piece wraps around the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
a herd is a crowd of animals
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: A writer finds himself with a beastly mob outside a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' is the verb, to pay romantic attention to, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood wrote the 1939 novel Goodbye to Berlin, the answer at 16 Across.

clue.text: Pain as the German misses problem with train

indicators.note: something that misses is left out, so letters are removed

blocks.note: a train coming off the rails
der is a German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A German traveller suffers when his train runs into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: DERAILMENT with the German article DER taken off its front.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is an illness or complaint, and a pain is a loose example of such a bodily trouble.

clue.text: As we may deduce, capital keeps leading man in order

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate, as does capital
a prior heads a religious order

explanation.surface: It reads like a deduction about a capital city holding the leading figure in its ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is the old adjective meaning excellent, so A1 (as AI), not a city. The 'order' is a monastic one.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from principles to conclusions by deduction, rather than from observed experience.

clue.text: Dance record slows in the middle

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a disc is a gramophone record
the central letter of five

explanation.surface: A dance track drops its tempo halfway through.
explanation.walkthrough: DISC is followed by the centre letter of 'slows'.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a dance event or club where recorded pop music is played, so a party for dancing.

clue.text: Big cod is out, no starter, cooked a treat

indicators.note: without its starter a word has lost its first letter
cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the word without its first letter

explanation.surface: A big cod is served up as a tasty meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish is a red herring: jumble BIG, COD, IS and UT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog biscuit is a hard baked snack given to a pet as a reward, which is what the word treat covers.

clue.text: Doctor Stone stores a Cremona for Brecht say

indicators.note: to store things is to keep them inside, so one piece sits within the others

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
st is the abbreviation for the stone weight
an Amati is a violin made by the Amati family of Cremona

explanation.surface: A doctor called Stone keeps a fine Italian violin for the playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Stone reads as a person's name, but each word is abbreviated separately. A Cremona is any violin from that town's great makers, such as the Amati family.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertolt Brecht was a German playwright, so he is an example of someone who writes plays for the stage.

clue.text: Raconteur terribly constipated with pressure lacking

indicators.note: lacking something means going without it, so a letter is removed
terribly suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A storyteller is dreadfully blocked up, unable to push.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the P from CONSTIPATED and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdotist tells anecdotes, short amusing stories, which is what a raconteur does skilfully in company.

clue.text: Novel of virtue corrected lie by Brontë

indicators.note: correcting something puts it into a different order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: virtuous is good
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A virtuous novel set out to put right a falsehood told by one of the Brontës.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brontë is not the definition's author: her name just supplies letters. GOOD is followed by a jumble of LIE BY BRONTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodbye to Berlin is Christopher Isherwood's 1939 book of linked stories about Weimar Berlin, later adapted as Cabaret.

clue.text: What some airlines do with surplus volume?

definitions.text: What some airlines do with surplus volume?

blocks.clueFragment: What some airlines do with surplus volume?
blocks.note: surface reading: carriers sell more seats than a flight holds when demand is heavy
setter's reading: a volume is a tome, and surplus means left over, so a spare tome

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: 'volume' reads as passenger numbers but is also a book, and 'surplus' is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Airlines overbook by selling more tickets than there are seats, expecting some passengers not to turn up.

clue.text: Lover dropped lawsuit for blackmail perhaps

blocks.note: a former partner who has been dropped is an ex
an action is a legal suit

explanation.surface: A jilted lover abandons a court case in favour of blackmail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped' belongs with 'Lover', describing a partner who has been dumped; it is not a deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is a demand for payment extracted by force or threat, and extortion by blackmail is one example.

clue.text: Boozer in Britain fuddled with ecstasy twice …

indicators.note: fuddled means confused, as if drunk, so the letters are muddled up

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the drug ecstasy, and there are two of them

explanation.surface: A British drinker is befuddled after taking ecstasy twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy. The ellipsis runs the story into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate, used as a noun, is a habitual drunkard, someone given to heavy drinking.

clue.text: Title accepted by the Spanish Crown Protector?

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
a title is the name of something

explanation.surface: A Spanish noble accepts a royal title as Lord Protector of the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crown is not royalty but the crown of a tooth, as the question mark hints.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooth enamel is the hard outer layer covering and shielding the crown, the visible part of a tooth.

clue.text: … died a dissolute man: Mr Gadwall?

blocks.note: d is the abbreviation for died
a rake is a dissolute man

explanation.surface: Continuing the drunk's story, he dies a debauched man named Mr Gadwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Gadwall reads as a surname, but a gadwall is a species of duck, and 'Mr' makes it the male.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, and the gadwall is a dabbling duck, so its Mr is a drake by example.

clue.text: Poet‘s Italian flower lady occasionally plucked

indicators.note: plucking now and then takes only every other letter

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, and the Arno flows through Florence
the first and third letters

explanation.surface: A poet's Italian blossom has its petals picked off by a lady now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword favourite for a river, something that flows. Matthew Arnold was the Victorian poet of Dover Beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold was a nineteenth-century English writer of verse and criticism, so an example of the word given.

clue.text: Whip caresses nude in film 16 Across inspired

indicators.note: to caress is to hold and stroke, so one piece embraces another

blocks.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip
nude means bare

explanation.surface: A racy film scene with a whip and a naked body.
explanation.walkthrough: The whip is the cat o' nine tails, the old naval lash. The surface fits the film's decadent Berlin nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret, the 1972 Bob Fosse film, was adapted via a stage musical from Isherwood's Berlin stories.

clue.text: Queen Cleopatra’s executioner to bow and scrape

blocks.note: R, for Regina, is the Latin for queen
Cleopatra killed herself with the bite of an asp

explanation.surface: Cleopatra's executioner is told to be servile before the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow and scrape' reads as fawning, but take it literally, as drawing a bow harshly across a string.
explanation.definitionFit: To rasp is to scrape roughly with a grating sound, as a badly drawn violin bow does.

clue.text: Villain being one for hero, friend to Caesar, J?

blocks.note: Mark Antony was Julius Caesar's ally
Caesar's initial J written after his surname, as in a list; his friend's initial is Mark's

explanation.surface: It poses a riddle about Caesar's friend being cast as a villain against a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is the register style: Julius Caesar as 'Caesar, J' pairs with Mark Antony as 'Antony, M'.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of opposite meaning, and villain is one for hero since the two are opposites.

clue.text: Yucatán native is permitted to answer

blocks.note: one who may do something is permitted to
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A local of the Mexican Yucatán is allowed to reply.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY is followed by A, the standard shorthand for answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maya are the indigenous people of the Yucatán peninsula and neighbouring Central America, builders of ancient cities.

clue.text: Clubs with high quality white earthenware

blocks.note: irons are golf clubs
tone is character or class, as in raising the tone

explanation.surface: Golf clubs come paired with fine white pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: The clubs are golf clubs, not a card suit. TONE is refinement, as in lowering the tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironstone china is a hard, dense, white English pottery first made in the early nineteenth century.

clue.text: Belly was so developed around large 16 Across character

indicators.note: something developed has grown into a new form, so the letters take a new order
being around something means enclosing it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone's stomach grew so much that it became a large figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange BELLY WAS SO around L for large.
explanation.definitionFit: Sally Bowles is the English cabaret singer in Isherwood's Goodbye to Berlin, later the star role in Cabaret.
